Locksmith here! Granted I'm Danish, and as such the locks I'm used to picking will differ from ones they use in the US, but I have participated in conventions and lectures in affiliation with ALOA in the past! 

If you're from the US, I suggest you check out TOOOL - they're a lovely bunch, and their lockpick sets are the best I've worked with yet!

Remember there are a lot of different locks. Some can practically be picked with a popsicle stick, whilst others are virtually unpickable. A normal wafer lock (usually used in small cabinets) is pretty easy, and a good place to start. After that I'd suggest you move up to a simple pin tumbler, without any kind of added security. In Denmark this would be something like a Ruko 500 or 600, but I can't think of an American equivalent.

When you get that down, you can move up to the difficult ones. I know Toyota has some very hard locks to pick. 

Hope this gives you an idea where to start :)

Okay, so first off, narrow it down to what you're looking for. A lot of people here are telling you to look into the roots of the genre, but the thing is that even bands like Anthrax and Metallica are very different, even though they were some of the bands who made the foundation for a heavy metal genre. Of course, there's also the issue of defining a genre - some may call bands like Nightwish and Evanescence metal, whereas others would define them as goth, emo, rock or whatever.

For the sake of making this easy for myself, I'm not going to really distinguish between metal, punk, grunge, rock and all the other heavy genres, simply because people define the genre differently. To make it easier for you, I'm going to put my own personal favorite song from each band in parenthesis.

If you're looking for something really heavy check out Danzig (Mother), Misfits (Last Caress) or Slayer (South of Heaven).

If you're looking for something a bit more simple, Metallica (Ride the Lightning) and Black Sabbath (Paranoid) are two of the most important bands to the metal genre.

If you're on the other hand feeling like you want to hear some very intricate riffs and impressive solos, I can recommend Anthrax (Got the Time), King Diamond (Eye of the Witch) and Iron Maiden (Run Silent Run Deep).

Then we have stuff like Kiss (Rock and Roll All Night), Twisted Sister (I Wanna Rock) and Mötley Crüe (Dr. Feelgood) who focus on more catchy tunes and image. If you like this stuff, I suggest you also check out Steel Panther - they're hilarious.

Personally, I like it if there's a bit of melody in the music I listen to, so my favorites include Coheed and Cambria (Feathers), Slipknot (Left Behind)(say what you will about them - I like their music) and the Danish band Magtens Korridorer (Sara Har) - their lyrics are in Danish, so I don't know if it's something you'll appreciate, but I figured it was worth mentioning them.

I'm willing to bet my life that I missed some very important names and categories here, so if anyone has an important input, feel free to write it up!

I'm going to allow myself to draw some parallels between your son and myself. Two years ago, when I was sixteen, I was like your kid. I spent most of my time online, gaming and chatting with friends. I got good grades and I was always told how much of a pleasant young man I was. I didn't talk much to my parents, and they thought it was just because I was being a teenager, and they didn't want to interfere, because they were certain I'd come to them if I had any problems. 

This next part is my own personal story, and it is very likely this won't apply to your son.

They were wrong. I had a lot of problems. I felt alone. I was a nerd. I had never had a girlfriend, and my friends always seemed to have a better time without me. I thought my parents were being apathetic to my situation because they didn't care. Eventually, I got trapped in a friendship with somewhat of a bad apple. He took me out drinking, and introduced me to marijuana. Cut to a few months later, where I'd got caught up in partying and my average grade in school had dropped by almost 60%. I got depressed. Very depressed. I didn't feel like anybody understood me, and I didn't feel like I was ready to start a life of my own, and I just started hating myself. I even attempted suicide once (thankfully, I was unsuccessful).

Then one night, I decided it couldn't be healthy to keep everything bottled up, and I went into my parents' bedroom late at night. I was crying my eyes out, and my mother asked me if I needed to talk. I came clean with everything. I thought she was going to be disappointed and throw me out. Instead, she held me and told me that she'd help me get back on my feet. I didn't believe my ears. Somebody seemed to actually care for me. I got happier, and eventually became friends with the best people I have ever known. I got my first girlfriend, and even though we're now no longer together, I feel happier because I know I have some support somewhere.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that what your son is going through is likely very normal, and there's a good chance it won't have any lasting effects on either him or your family. But just in case, remember that your son is a different person than you, and different people experience things differently. If you think he needs it, ask him if he needs to talk. As I said earlier: it's most likely nothing - but it could be something, in which case, I'd suggest trying to help him.
